cases.caseName: Orissa Mining Corporation Ltd. v. Ministry of Environment & Forest & Ors.
cases.ratioDecidendi: A mining lease on Scheduled Areas cannot be granted without the free, prior and informed consent of the gram sabha under Section 4(1) of the FRA 2006, triggered by Articles 244 and 344(1) protective framework.

cases.caseName: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India (Privacy-9J)
cases.ratioDecidendi: The right to privacy is a fundamental right flowing from Article 21, subject to a three-part proportionality test: legality, legitimate aim, and necessity/proportionality of state action.

cases.caseName: K.S. Puttaswamy (Aadhaar-5J) v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Aadhaar upheld as constitutional but only as a targeted, proportionality-checked identification system; it cannot be extended through indefinite or disproportionate state surveillance.

cases.caseName: Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Internet shutdown orders under the IT Act 2000 are not above judicial review; they must satisfy necessity and proportionality and be published without delay, else they violate Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g).

cases.caseName: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Section 66A of the IT Act 2000 struck down as void under Article 19(2) for vagueness; only speech within clearly defined restrictions may be restricted, preserving the right to criticise government.

cases.caseName: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (Basic Structure-13J)
cases.ratioDecidendi: Parliament cannot amend the Constitution so as to destroy or damage its basic structure, including the rule of law, judicial review, and dignity-based rights.

cases.caseName: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Article 21 procedure must be 'fair, just and reasonable', merging the rights to life, freedom and equality; arbitrary executive procedure cannot deprive a person of liberty.

cases.caseName: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation (Pavement Dwellers)
cases.ratioDecidendi: Eviction of slum/pavement dwellers deprives them of their livelihood and violates Article 21; they may be moved only with notice, opportunity of hearing, and humane consideration for alternative accommodation.

cases.caseName: Sudama Singh v. Government of Delhi & Ors.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Jhuggi-jhopri dwellers are entitled to resettlement before demolition; relocation must be preceded by transparent survey, identification and notice, consistent with Article 21 that they not be rendered homeless.
statutoryProvisions: Delhi Slum and JJ Rehabilitation Policies

cases.caseName: Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation v. Nawab Khan Gulab Khan
cases.ratioDecidendi: Municipalities cannot evict citizens from hutments without following due process; slum dwellers holding municipal 'passes' or settled long-term user acquires a protectable right against summary displacement.

cases.caseName: P.G. Gupta v. State of Gujarat (Oustees)
cases.ratioDecidendi: Displaced oustees of development projects are entitled to rehabilitation and compensation packages; forced eviction absent a scheme of resettlement violates Article 21.

cases.caseName: Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Environmental law rests on sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter-pays principle; they are part of Article 21's right to a clean environment.

cases.caseName: Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India (Bichhri)
cases.ratioDecidendi: Industries generating hazardous pollution must pay remediation costs (polluter-pays), and the legal-aid doctrine supports the State's duty to ensure clean environment under Article 21.

cases.caseName: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Ganga Pollution Matter)
cases.ratioDecidendi: The right to life under Article 21 includes the right to a pollution-free environment; courts can direct closure of offending units and award exemplary damages for environmental harm.

cases.caseName: T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad v. Union of India (Forest Case)
cases.ratioDecidendi: The term 'forest' must be given its widest dictionary meaning; all forest lands require prior central approval for non-forest use under the Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, and timber extraction needs prior permission.

cases.caseName: Sterlite Industries (India) Ltd. v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Environmental clearances and factory siting must respect ecologically sensitive areas; the precautionary approach requires a demonstrated balance between industrial need and environmental harm.

cases.caseName: Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar
cases.ratioDecidendi: The right to live in a healthy environment and be free from hazardous pollution is part of Article 21; public-spirited citizens may approach courts for its vindication.

cases.caseName: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: The State must take positive measures to protect labour from bondage and exploitation; Article 21 obligates decent working conditions and the rehabilitation of bonded workers.

cases.caseName: People's Union for Democratic Rights v. Union of India (Asiad Workers)
cases.ratioDecidendi: Non-payment of minimum wages to construction workers violates Articles 21 and 23; the State must enforce labour welfare statutes and cannot ignore systematic violations by contractors.

cases.caseName: Consumer Education & Research Centre v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Article 21 guarantees the right to health of workers; every occupier/employer must ensure safe working conditions and health safeguards, and workers are entitled to compensation for occupational disease.

statutes.citation: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006
statutes.name: FRA 2006

sections.title: Gram Sabha consent
sections.principle: No diversion of forest rights over Scheduled Areas is valid without resolution of the concerned gram sabha, by a majority of the members present, which shall be the authority to initiate the process for determining the nature and extent of individual or community forest rights.

sections.title: Limitation of rights
sections.principle: The gram sabha resolution shall be made in conformity with ensuring customary rights, and must not in any way be in contravention of the spirit of the Act.

sections.title: Duties
sections.principle: Holders of forest rights are duty-bound to protect forests, wildlife and habitat alongside the exercise of their rights.

sections.title: Restriction on de-reservation/use
sections.principle: No State Government or authority may de-reserve a forest or permit any forest land for non-forest purpose, without the prior approval of the Central Government.

sections.title: Power to restrict industrial activity
sections.principle: The Central Government may take measures to protect and improve the environment, including restricting areas for industries and operations in ecologically sensitive locations.

sections.title: Directions
sections.principle: The Central Government may issue directions for closure or regulation of an industry operating in violation of the Act, including in emergencies.

statutes.citation: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
statutes.name: Water Act 1974

sections.title: Prohibition on pollution
sections.principle: No person shall knowingly permit any poisonous, noxious or polluting matter to enter any stream or well, otherwise than in compliance with standards and consent conditions.

sections.title: Direction for interception or blocking
sections.principle: The Government may direct interception, monitoring or blocking of any information for reasons of sovereignty, security, public order or incitement, subject to procedure and record of reasons.

sections.title: Blocking of public access
sections.principle: Public access may be blocked in the interest of sovereignty, integrity, defence, security, foreign relations or public order, by following the statutory procedure under the 2009 Rules.

sections.title: Intermediary safe harbour
sections.principle: An intermediary is not liable for third-party information if it acts only as a conduit and complies with due diligence and takedown duties.

statutes.citation: Telecom Suspension and Revocation Rules, 2017 (as amended 2022)
statutes.name: Telecom Suspension Rules 2017

sections.title: Suspension orders
sections.principle: Orders suspending telecom services must be issued on limited grounds and remain effective only for as long as the emergency or threat to public order subsists.

sections.title: Review
sections.principle: A review committee shall examine every suspension order and directions shall continue only upon approval; indefinite suspensions are impermissible.

sections.title: Publication
sections.principle: Suspension orders must be communicated and published to ensure citizens can challenge them.

statutes.citation: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
statutes.name: RFCTLARR Act 2013

sections.title: Lapse of old acquisitions
sections.principle: Land acquisition proceedings under the 1894 Act that remained uncompleted with possession not taken and compensation unpaid lapse, and fresh proceedings must be undertaken under the 2013 Act.

sections.title: Notice to interested persons
sections.principle: Duly-notified public hearings on objections and social impact are mandatory before an area is declared a 'public purpose' acquisition.

sections.title: Affected family
sections.principle: Defines affected families broadly to include those whose lands are acquired and those primarily dependent on the land including informal dwellers.

sections.title: Gig worker
sections.principle: Defines gig worker as a worker who performs work or participates in a work arrangement outside of a traditional employer-employee relationship.

sections.title: Platform worker
sections.principle: Defines platform worker as a gig worker whose work is enabled by an online platform that offers goods or services to the public, including delivery and mobility apps.

sections.title: SSP benefits for gig workers
sections.principle: Provides for registration and social security (health, old age, accident) for gig and platform workers through aggregator contributions and a central Social Security Fund.

sections.title: Aggregator
sections.principle: An aggregator is a digital intermediary that enables a consumer to connect with a driver or delivery partner, covering delivery and ride-hailing apps.

sections.title: Application
sections.principle: Guidelines apply to all aggregators operating ride-hailing and delivery through digitally-enabled transport networks.

sections.title: Driver treatment
sections.principle: Aggregators shall not terminate or deactivate driver-partner accounts without a fair and documented hearing process.
